Review Body: What a read, and what a fun time it was learning about all this. Took awhile to admit but I do suffer from my time spent at war in the Middle East. Seeing what part of your brain is doing what, whenever you recall these memories is something you can’t put a price on. This will definitely help those that want an acute understanding of what’s going in their bodies whenever they face or run away from their demons. My only gripe is I’ve never read a book in the early chapters that said “we’ll discuss subject X later in chapter X” as much as this one. A sigh will escape you while a subject has you enthralled, only for it not to be explained until further in the book. This is gonna happen a lot. Still a wellspring of information and a fascinating book. Definitely recommend if you yourself suffer from scars no one else can see and want to take steps in healing yourself.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on April 17, 2015
Review Body:
Before the brain-based work became known to me, I spent 25 years in therapy for lifelong depression, anxiety, and suicidal thoughts and was told by various practitioners that they guessed I wasn't "ready to change." In the past 5 years, I started reading about PTSD in some psychology books I happened to be editing and realized that I had every identifying trait. I began seeing a therapist who immediately pinpointed my trauma and its importance. I've read many other authors on the subject, starting with Judith Herman.
"The Body Keeps the Score," with its more-detailed information of the effects of trauma on a young brain and broader description of associated behavior traits, has had an incredible impact on my psyche. After 50+ years of blaming myself---self-branding as "Loser"--- for not being able to overcome my emotional problems and accomplish what I know I'm capable of, I now see the whole picture clearly. I see that I was in essence handicapped by immobilizing fear as a product of a terrifying environment that looked fine from the outside. What did I have to be unhappy about?
This book helped me wrap the garbage in a Hefty bag and tie it up with a ribbon. My depression, constant anxiety, and self-loathing have lifted to a great extent and I'm beginning to learn how to take care of myself. Safety first!
I can't say how it measures up from a professional/researcher standpoint, but as a tool for the average person who's willing to put the time in to reading it, I can't say enough about it and the hope it's given me. Thank-you Dr. van der Kolk.

RE: The comment in the Amazon review by G.V. Price, about it not presenting the entire "warts and all" story of trauma: I say trauma sufferers are all too familiar with the warts, and moving on to "the promise" is a welcome change.
